question: How should we classify the work before deciding what to feature?
context: Share mixes original work, variants, editable resources and finished exports. A piece can serve several uses. The first pass should help us find the right item for a real campaign without confusing a derivative with its source.
target: Pick the most useful first classification layer for retrieving one owned, eligible item for a named editorial or practical job. Use the material described. Work may fit several views.

options.title: What a person can do with it
options.pitch: Tag items by use: open a working example, edit a source, use a palette, watch a result or learn a workflow.
options.outcome: A campaign or search can start with the action it wants someone to take.
options.pro: Useful to both an editor and a visitor.
options.con: Requires an editorial judgement beyond file metadata.

options.title: Original, alternate, crop or finished export
options.pitch: Group by source project and record the relationship between usable originals and their output variants.
options.outcome: Search and campaign prep surface distinct pieces before repeats of the same asset.
options.pro: Makes attribution and editability easier to see.
options.con: Legacy items may lack a dependable source link.

options.title: What can be reused and where
options.pitch: Classify view-only, downloadable, editable and cleared for public promotion using current rights and visibility.
options.outcome: Eligible material can be found without guessing about rights.
options.pro: Supports responsible reuse and publication.
options.con: Eligibility alone cannot establish creative relevance.

options.title: Campaign and message
options.pitch: Tag release proofs, build stories, reusable resources and invitations as separate editorial uses.
options.outcome: Editors can assemble a relevant set for each campaign.
options.pro: Maps directly to editorial briefs.
options.con: The same piece needs multiple tags over time.

options.title: Format and crop readiness
options.pitch: Classify stills, video and editable files by available dimensions, square or portrait crops and caption support.
options.outcome: Editors know which versions can go into a social placement or a product page.
options.pro: Some attributes can be detected from the files.
options.con: A correctly sized file can still be the wrong subject.

question: Which campaigns can we make from work that already exists?
context: Composer can run several campaigns in parallel. Each option has its own audience, message, proof and destination. Selecting a campaign can start a separate round of artwork choices later.
target: Rank viable independent campaigns on audience fit, concrete proof, useful destination and distinctiveness. No option excludes the others. Consider what can be substantiated today.

options.title: Build and own a working app
options.pitch: For builders who want ownership. Show one live app beside its source and deployment path. Send people to its reproducible build.
options.outcome: A new builder can see what ownership looks like and take a first step.
options.pro: Serves the core Composer promise.
options.con: A weak example makes the promise feel abstract.

options.title: Watch the cut, see the edit
options.pitch: For creators. Pair a finished Media Studio piece with its actual edit or alternate and a direct playback link.
options.outcome: People can judge the creative work and follow how it was made.
options.pro: The output leads and product proof follows.
options.con: Needs a cleared, genuinely useful source comparison.

options.title: Pick up a resource and use it
options.pitch: For designers and builders. Feature one rights-checked editable file or palette and link straight to the resource and its source.
options.outcome: A reader receives something useful in one click.
options.pro: Each card has a practical reason to exist.
options.con: Requires eligible originals and deliberate selection every time.

options.title: Make today’s small job easier
options.pitch: Run separate utility posts around Spin’s live wheel and Paperwork’s fictional sample. Each post opens its own tool.
options.outcome: People can try an immediate task without learning the wider platform.
options.pro: Demonstrates genuine working software.
options.con: Requires care to keep the individual app identities recognisable.

options.title: Choose the original
options.pitch: For artists who work in variants. Use Prints Desktop and the published Pick the Original material to show a real selection or source trail.
options.outcome: Creators see the product address a recognisable creative step.
options.pro: Specific comparison makes the story memorable.
options.con: Exports must show which interface, platform and source are available.

question: Which working example should lead the Composer homepage?
context: The homepage already links to first-app setup and real apps. These choices take the live-app direction further by choosing what a newcomer can actually open and what it proves.
target: Choose a lead example for a first-time indie builder who should be able to use it and trace how to build or own something like it. Consider immediate use, representativeness and risk of distraction.

options.title: Hello from source to live deployment
options.pitch: Show the smallest owned Cloudflare app, its exact starter source and the Get Ready path.
options.outcome: A builder can reproduce the first success with minimal prerequisites.
options.pro: Closely matches the beginner workflow Composer supports.
options.con: Needs excellent presentation because the product result is intentionally small.

options.title: The connected Guestbook and Linkarooie demo
options.pitch: Show a postcard in its source app and the approved item appearing in the connected app.
options.outcome: People see independent apps working together with a concrete handoff.
options.pro: Explains what Composer adds beyond a scaffold.
options.con: Two apps and moderation take more explanation.

options.title: Spin a real wheel
options.pitch: Let someone run a wheel, then show how the independently deployed app is sourced and maintained.
options.outcome: The opening provides a memorable hands-on result within seconds.
options.pro: A stranger already knows what to try.
options.con: The simple interaction does not show how Composer joins multiple apps.

options.title: Sign Paperwork’s fictional sample
options.pitch: Open the actual sample, fill it and download a finished file. Link to the independent build.
options.outcome: A builder sees a complete and recognisable task before reading setup docs.
options.pro: Shows a product with a clear ownership and privacy story.
options.con: A signing-first hook can make people mistake Composer for a PDF product.

options.title: A Media Studio cut with the source path
options.pitch: Open the published film and its process, then link to the related Studio build.
options.outcome: Creative users see the kind of system and output Composer can support.
options.pro: Gives the opening an expressive real result.
options.con: Heavier than a first deployed app and narrower for non-video builders.

question: What should Show me something useful do in Share?
context: A visitor should reach a source-backed resource without trawling repeated variants. Signed-in feedback should help us learn where people get stuck. Compare what would go in the first screen.
target: Choose a first-screen flow for finding something specific to reuse or explore. Prefer choices with a clear link to source and a practical way to test missing discovery.

options.title: Start with an editable file, palette or print
options.pitch: Give each job one intentionally chosen example, a direct opening and a route to more of that type.
options.outcome: A visitor with no query can reach a practical result.
options.pro: Makes the reason for each featured item explicit.
options.con: Needs a regularly refreshed selection.

options.title: Choose a project, then see the originals
options.pitch: Show distinct project starts and collapse crops and variants under their source item.
options.outcome: A visitor can explore a recognisable body of work without seeing the same piece repeatedly.
options.pro: Keeps credit and provenance visible.
options.con: People may know the task and have no project in mind.

options.title: Search by topic, format and reuse
options.pitch: Show results as people filter, with original, downloadable and editable clearly labelled.
options.outcome: A visitor with a clear request can rule items in or out quickly.
options.pro: Works across many projects and campaign types.
options.con: Depends on clean classification and a useful fallback for empty results.

options.title: Continue from work you liked
options.pitch: Surface the signed-in shortlist next to relevant original items, with control over what counts as similar.
options.outcome: Repeat visits start from preferences the owner has already expressed.
options.pro: Uses actual feedback instead of general popularity.
options.con: Needs enough deliberate signals and a sensible signed-out alternative.

options.title: Show what a failed search missed
options.pitch: Make zero-result recovery visible and let a signed-in owner send the failed query with a note.
options.outcome: The catalogue gets specific examples of useful items people could not find.
options.pro: Produces actionable feedback tied to a real failure.
options.con: Improves search quality over time rather than offering a strong browse lead itself.

question: Which real Studio workflow is worth a feature?
context: The Studio already publishes work across video, alternate cuts and browser tools. Pick an existing example with a visibly different input and outcome, then decide what still needs to be shown.
target: Choose a credible flagship workflow with a usable destination, visible inputs and outputs, and an honest explanation of what the tool did. Rank an actual cut or walkthrough above abstract polish.

sources.label: Pick the Original in Prints Desktop

options.title: Low Tide in the 30-second Studio film
options.pitch: Open with the real LoftwahFM artwork, show where it appears in the cut, and link to the published teaser.
options.outcome: A viewer sees how original material feeds the final piece.
options.pro: A tight, tangible example with playable proof.
options.con: The teaser needs a short process inset for the feature to teach anything.

options.title: The 82-second owned Studio walkthrough
options.pitch: Use the existing sequence from brief to saved takes, then show its published export in the same feature.
options.outcome: A viewer sees how a project moves through a working studio.
options.pro: Proves the broad workflow with an existing recording.
options.con: Requires a short first view so the opening has a single story.

options.title: A real alternate cut next to the one that shipped
options.pitch: Show the published Pick the Original case with a source-linked comparison and attribute the Prints Desktop workflow accurately.
options.outcome: A viewer understands the creative judgement and where to inspect the source.
options.pro: There is a real decision to discuss.
options.con: Needs cleared alternate material and a precise distinction between the tools.

options.title: A LoftwahFM music video with a visible edit decision
options.pitch: Feature Change the Default if we can show a meaningful cut or staging decision alongside playback.
options.outcome: A viewer gets the completed work and one concrete editing lesson.
options.pro: Connects two projects around original published output.
options.con: The process requires relevant cleared material. Playback alone does not prove the editor workflow.

question: Which Paperwork job should we show in one complete example?
context: Paperwork has a fictional sample, native fillable fields, browser-local signing and a saved PDF. Each option proposes a visible start and finish for the current product.
target: Pick the most useful demonstration for somebody arriving with a PDF. Weigh sample-to-own-document transfer, privacy and reliable completion.

options.title: Fill and sign the fictional garden form
options.pitch: Walk from the visible fields to signature placement and download using the existing sample.
options.outcome: A first-time signer can rehearse the workflow without uploading a personal file.
options.pro: Shows the real UI without exposing personal data.
options.con: A fillable sample does not explain scanned forms.

options.title: Write onto a scanned form
options.pitch: Choose a cleared fictional scan, place text and a signature and verify the exported page.
options.outcome: Users understand what to do when a PDF has no interactive fields.
options.pro: Solves a specific, common moment of confusion.
options.con: Needs a representative fictional scan and phone-friendly placement.

options.title: Drop a PDF and sign it once
options.pitch: Use a disposable file to show drop-to-sign, single-use signature and local download.
options.outcome: A repeat signer sees the most direct path from file to signed copy.
options.pro: Demonstrates the newest practical shortcut.
options.con: An example must make starting over and finding the resulting file obvious.

options.title: Prepare a printable copy
options.pitch: Show the completed fictional print-shop example, then verify print or download preview.
options.outcome: A person preparing a paper copy knows what the output looks like.
options.pro: Makes the final deliverable visible.
options.con: Actual printers and OS print flows vary.

question: What should Spin prove in its first ten seconds?
context: The product is the functioning wheel. The project also has presets, a custom entry path and a result explanation. Choose which working experience deserves the strongest art and interaction treatment.
target: Rank the first-run Spin flows for immediate understanding and expressive character. Preserve practical editing and inspectable outcomes. Avoid treating generic decoration as working evidence.

options.title: Spin immediately, then change the inputs
options.pitch: Start with a playable preset. Put the large wheel, editable choices and a distinct result in the same first run.
options.outcome: A new visitor experiences the core action before setting anything up.
options.pro: The liveliest visual is the working wheel.
options.con: Sample entries need an obvious replacement path.

options.title: Paste a real list and spin it
options.pitch: Start with a clearly labelled multiline entry box and update the wheel as items appear.
options.outcome: Visitors with a list reach their own result quickly.
options.pro: Shows immediate personal usefulness.
options.con: An empty opening needs a playable example for browsing visitors.

options.title: Choose an occasion and play
options.pitch: Give examples such as food or entertainment their own small illustration and one-click playable wheel.
options.outcome: Someone with a casual decision starts from an understandable preset.
options.pro: Gives the mini-app several recognisable uses and campaign subjects.
options.con: Artwork and presets can delay the first action if given too much space.

options.title: Show a result worth sharing or checking
options.pitch: Follow one sample spin into its result, replay and checked-result explanation.
options.outcome: A visitor sees why the result can travel beyond the page.
options.pro: Demonstrates what distinguishes Spin from a decorative spinner.
options.con: The proof belongs after a real spin, where the context is clear.

question: What has to be true before a public card earns the lead?
context: The social card, homepage and catalogue have different jobs. Compare how to choose and verify an asset after the campaign is defined.
target: Choose the editorial checks most likely to catch an irrelevant or weak feature before publication. Prefer checks grounded in a real asset, placement and next action.

options.title: Name what the person gets after the click
options.pitch: Pick the actual resource, output or working page before making the card.
options.outcome: Design starts from something worth opening.
options.pro: Rejects interchangeable artwork early.
options.con: Requires a working, useful destination.

options.title: Compare the real placements
options.pitch: View the same candidate at feed size, a narrow phone opening and its target export crop.
options.outcome: Weak subjects or unreadable copy become apparent before release.
options.pro: Tests the thing people will see.
options.con: Needs completed candidates rather than written concepts.

options.title: Check identity and original colours
options.pitch: Use the approved mark and exact brand colour. Keep white, neutral and original source colours true where intended.
options.outcome: The work reads as the right app and keeps the subject clear.
options.pro: Catches the muddied-colour failure the earlier graphics showed.
options.con: Correct colours alone cannot establish a compelling idea.

options.title: Verify the asset, credit and reuse state
options.pitch: Trace the piece to its real source and confirm permission for the intended placement.
options.outcome: The card can link to and properly credit the original.
options.pro: Protects continuity between discovery and publication.
options.con: Requires review when provenance is incomplete.

options.title: Compare two genuinely different subjects
options.pitch: Render a product-result lead and an editorial or art-led choice at equal size. Judge the actual pixels and useful action separately.
options.outcome: The stronger subject can win before a styling preference dominates.
options.pro: Invites real creative alternatives.
options.con: Takes an extra candidate and an explicit result to compare.

question: What should a new Prints user finish in the first session?
context: Prints Desktop can browse source-linked artwork, compare work, and export with a source connection. Its first task should end with something the user can inspect.
target: Choose a credible first-session task supported by the current release. Prefer a visible result and avoid promising platform coverage or authorisations that remain untested.

options.title: Compare original and alternate
options.pitch: Open two real cleared versions and decide which one to keep.
options.outcome: A creator sees how Prints supports a judgement they already make.
options.pro: Has a recognisable start and finish.
options.con: Needs an understandable pair and lacks the source-link demonstration.

options.title: Open one result and trace its source
options.pitch: Follow the link from an existing image into the owning material and project.
options.outcome: A creator can verify where their work came from.
options.pro: Proves traceability quickly.
options.con: A successful browse can feel passive unless the assets are carefully chosen.

options.title: Make a source-linked export
options.pitch: Pick a cleared image, export it and open the result to inspect the attached source reference.
options.outcome: The first session leaves a usable result the creator can verify.
options.pro: Proves a distinct practical feature.
options.con: Requires a representative export path and accurate platform guidance.

options.title: Watch the walkthrough, then repeat one step
options.pitch: Use a short excerpt of Pick the Original, followed by a direct task in Prints.
options.outcome: A creator sees why the task matters before doing it.
options.pro: Pairs a published example with practice.
options.con: The extra viewing step slows a user who came ready to work.

question: Which listening or viewing experience should the next LoftwahFM post open?
context: The catalogue has full records, videos and station listening. The next post needs an identifiable work and a destination worth opening.
target: Rank the concrete invitations for an interested listener, considering available published work, time commitment and clear destination. Do not infer listener preference from the catalogue.

sources.label: Who Keeps the Map? and its music videos

options.title: Open Who Gets the Change’s Encore Cut
options.pitch: Lead with a specific shot from the released video and go straight to playable video.
options.outcome: A listener can see the performance and hear the track together.
options.pro: Gives the post a single recognisable moment.
options.con: The shot must carry meaning in a muted preview.

options.title: Watch Change the Default in context
options.pitch: Lead with the story’s pivotal action and send viewers to the playable music video and album context.
options.outcome: An interested viewer can follow the story into the record.
options.pro: Connects a real film and song release.
options.con: Needs a clear opening frame and avoids giving away too much.

options.title: Start the album and follow its sequence
options.pitch: Use the real album cover and send listeners to the record at track one.
options.outcome: Visitors reach the listening experience the record was assembled to provide.
options.pro: Keeps the album rather than a single clip at the centre.
options.con: Asks for more time from a first-time listener.

options.title: Hear the work in the station
options.pitch: Use a real programmed set with an honest schedule or entry, then link to listening.
options.outcome: Listeners discover the track as part of the station.
options.pro: Builds awareness of what makes LoftwahFM a station.
options.con: Needs an actual accessible set and a fallback when the track is no longer on air.

question: Which product journey should we prove next in the actual app?
context: Several projects have recent code or releases and specific gaps in the real user journey. A proof here means someone can do a meaningful thing with the current product and we can show it clearly.
target: Rank concrete next proofs with user consequence and a clear completion criterion. Use stated known limits. Do not assume traffic, access, device or release status beyond the supplied context.

options.title: One newcomer builds an app they can open
options.pitch: Use the Get Ready path and actual starter. End on their live domain with its exact source.
options.outcome: We can locate the first place a new builder gets stuck and show a reproducible success.
options.pro: Directly tests Composer’s main promise.
options.con: Requires a fresh environment and appropriate deployment access.

options.title: Two players join, finish and rematch in Protocol 11
options.pitch: Follow an actual room across two clients, with a reconnect and one rematch.
options.outcome: Players can return to a working match without losing the result.
options.pro: Tests the concurrency work where players feel it.
options.con: Needs the relevant release, two clients and the correct account state.

options.title: An approved newcomer enters Foilbury
options.pitch: Follow a fictional access request through approval, then open the collection with the intended account.
options.outcome: The invitation model becomes understandable and testable end to end.
options.pro: Checks the boundary as experienced by a newcomer.
options.con: Needs a legitimate test identity and preserves the abuse and spend controls.

options.title: Play one match worth showing
options.pitch: Record a real satisfying first match, use the original Bubblecap identity, and compare player-facing screenshots at phone size.
options.outcome: The public opening can show the feel of the actual game in one short sequence.
options.pro: Builds from known creative evidence and real play.
options.con: A good recording cannot stand in for play and control checks.

options.title: Complete the intended SHOALSHOT flow on an iPhone
options.pitch: Run a physical-device session with the current version and capture the relevant interaction and recovery.
options.outcome: The team can isolate device-specific failures and see what a handheld user sees.
options.pro: Addresses a verification gap that screenshots and simulators cannot close.
options.con: Requires appropriate physical-device access.

question: Where should feedback enter the work so it actually changes the next attempt?
context: The first review put comments in a separate admin screen. The most useful feedback names the real page, artwork or job where the problem appeared and stays attached to it.
target: Choose which feedback routes would most reliably give agents actionable, owner-controlled notes with the right project context. Compare quick point-of-use feedback with deliberate decisions.

options.title: Give feedback on the page you’re using
options.pitch: Put a signed-in action on Share and other priority surfaces with explicit page and optional item context.
options.outcome: Notes can be captured as soon as a real problem appears.
options.pro: Preserves the moment and location of the problem.
options.con: Needs a privacy boundary and unobtrusive public layout.

options.title: Comment on the exact candidate
options.pitch: Attach a note to a draft, preview or social variant, including the actual crop being viewed.
options.outcome: An agent can see what the note refers to before revising it.
options.pro: Avoids confusing a comment on one crop with judgement of the whole design.
options.con: Needs stable candidate IDs and accessible preview versions.

options.title: Add context while answering the decision
options.pitch: Keep a note on each question, whether or not an option fits. Give the owner a way to point out missing alternatives.
options.outcome: The next brief can take constraints and gaps into account.
options.pro: Works for considered choices and refusals.
options.con: Feedback arrives only if someone opens the brief.

options.title: Review notes and assign the owning GitHub issue
options.pitch: Use a private triage view to place a public-safe summary and evidence link into the right issue.
options.outcome: Reported problems have an owner and a visible follow-up.
options.pro: Makes it harder for a useful report to get lost.
options.con: Adds a step and requires care around private content.
